name: tag-group
title: TagGroup
description: The sheet's .ds-tag: a 12px uppercase chip, in the seven treatments the sheet defines — which is why there are seven.

files.content: import { createContext, useContext } from 'react' import { Button as AriaButton, Label as AriaLabel, Tag as AriaTag, TagGroup as AriaTagGroup, TagList as AriaTagList, } from 'react-aria-components' import type { LabelProps as AriaLabelProps, TagGroupProps as AriaTagGroupProps, TagListProps as AriaTagListProps, TagProps as AriaTagProps, } from 'react-aria-components' import { LABEL } from '../field' /** * The sheet's `.ds-tag`: a 12px uppercase chip with a transparent 1px edge, so every variant is the * same box however it is filled. * * **The hover state is `:hover`, not `data-hovered`.** React Aria's `Tag` does not provide one — * a real pointer hover leaves the tag without the attribute, which this component's own test caught. * Everywhere else in this system `data-[hovered]` is right because React Aria supplies it; here the * only honest source of "the pointer is on this chip" is the browser's own pseudo-class. * * The hover recipe is the same one the button uses — the tag's own colour deepened toward ink — and * for the same reason. The sheet brightens its chips with `filter: brightness(1.08)`, which is * invisible on a fill that already sits near the top of its range and says nothing at all about * *which* tag you are pointing at. `--tag-hover` is declared by each variant and read here, so the * recipe and the base land on the same element. */ export const CHIP = [ 'inline-flex items-center', 'border rounded-md px-2.5 py-1', 'text-[12px] tracking-[-0.01em] uppercase', 'transition-[color,background-color,border-color] duration-[120ms] ease-pulse', ].join(' ') export const TAG_CHIP = [ CHIP, 'cursor-pointer', 'hover:bg-(--tag-hover)', 'data-[pressed]:bg-(--tag-pressed)', 'data-[focus-visible]:outline-1 data-[focus-visible]:outline-offset-2', 'data-[focus-visible]:outline-ring', 'data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed data-[disabled]:opacity-40', // A tag with a remove button is still one chip, so the button sits inside the box rather than // beside it. '[&[data-rac]]:select-none', ].join(' ') /** * The sheet's `.ds-tag--*`, one per variant it defines — seven, because that is how many it has. * * `default` and `outline` are the two outlines, and `outline` is the one the sheet gives the accent * on hover. The three fills carry `ink`. The two accented outlines take a wash of their own colour, * which is the same "derive from the base" rule the fills follow — an outline has no fill to deepen, * so it gains one. * * Every one of these is written out in full rather than built from a template string: Tailwind reads * source text, and `var(--color-${token})` is not source text it can see. */ const VARIANT: Record = { default: 'border-transparent text-foreground/70 hover:text-foreground', outline: 'border-input text-foreground/70 hover:border-primary hover:text-primary', teal: '[--tag:var(--color-primary)] [--tag-hover:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-primary)_88%,var(--color-ink))] [--tag-pressed:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-primary)_78%,var(--color-ink))] border-transparent bg-(--tag) text-ink', gray: '[--tag:var(--color-secondary)] [--tag-hover:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-secondary)_88%,var(--color-ink))] [--tag-pressed:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-secondary)_78%,var(--color-ink))] border-transparent bg-(--tag) text-ink', yellow: '[--tag:var(--color-warning)] [--tag-hover:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-warning)_88%,var(--color-ink))] [--tag-pressed:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-warning)_78%,var(--color-ink))] border-transparent bg-(--tag) text-ink', 'outline-ring': '[--tag-hover:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-primary)_14%,transparent)] [--tag-pressed:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-primary)_22%,transparent)] border-primary text-primary', 'outline-warning': '[--tag-hover:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-warning)_14%,transparent)] [--tag-pressed:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-warning)_22%,transparent)] border-warning text-warning', } export type TagVariant = | 'default' | 'outline' | 'teal' | 'gray' | 'yellow' | 'outline-ring' | 'outline-warning' /** * The label inside a tag, and the anchor it becomes when the tag has an `href`. React Aria reports a * tag with an `href` as `data-href` on a grid row and renders no anchor itself — the same as its * navigation tree — so the destination is drawn here. A tag is a real link or it is a chip, and * `middle-click`, "open in a new tab" and the status bar all need the anchor. */ const LINK = 'inline-flex min-w-0 items-center text-inherit no-underline' const HREF = createContext(undefined) /** * The remove button, drawn when the group allows removing. React Aria marks the tag * `data-allows-removing` and leaves the control to the consumer, exactly as it does for the tree's * disclosure — so this writes it, for the same reason `Table.Selection` writes its own slot: the one * attribute that makes it work is the one nobody remembers. */ export const TAG_REMOVE = [ 'ms-1.5 -me-1 grid size-3.5 shrink-0 cursor-pointer place-items-center', 'text-current opacity-55', 'transition-opacity duration-[120ms] ease-pulse', 'hover:opacity-100', 'data-[focus-visible]:outline-1 data-[focus-visible]:outline-offset-1', 'data-[focus-visible]:outline-current', ].join(' ') /** The list wraps, because chips that overflow a column are the one thing a tag group is for. */ const LIST = 'flex flex-wrap gap-2' // Not generic, unlike `TagListProps`: React Aria's own `TagGroupProps` is not — a tag group's items // are tags, and the group itself owns no data of its own. export interface TagGroupProps extends Omit< AriaTagGroupProps, | 'children' | 'className' | 'selectionMode' | 'selectedKeys' | 'defaultSelectedKeys' | 'onSelectionChange' | 'disabledKeys' | 'onRemove' > { /** `none`, `single` or `multiple`. */ selectionMode?: AriaTagGroupProps['selectionMode'] /** The chosen chips, by each tag's `id`. */ selectedKeys?: AriaTagGroupProps['selectedKeys'] /** What starts chosen. */ defaultSelectedKeys?: AriaTagGroupProps['defaultSelectedKeys'] /** Called with the new set of keys. */ onSelectionChange?: AriaTagGroupProps['onSelectionChange'] /** Chips that cannot be chosen. */ disabledKeys?: AriaTagGroupProps['disabledKeys'] /** Called when a chip's remove button is pressed. */ onRemove?: AriaTagGroupProps['onRemove'] /** `className` places the group; the chips' own styling stays internal. */ className?: string /** A `TagGroup.Label`, then a `TagGroup.List`. */ children?: React.ReactNode } export interface TagGroupLabelProps extends AriaLabelProps { children?: React.ReactNode } export interface TagGroupListProps extends Omit< AriaTagListProps, 'className' > { className?: string children?: React.ReactNode } export interface TagProps extends Omit { /** Which of the sheet's chips this is. */ variant?: TagVariant /** * Turns the chip into a link. React Aria matches it, and this component draws the anchor — a tag * with an `href` is a grid row with `data-href` and nothing to click otherwise. */ href?: string className?: string children?: React.ReactNode } /** * The group's legend. Use it as `TagGroup.Label`, above a `TagGroup.List`. * * Exported as `TagGroupLabel` only so tooling can resolve it; consume the compound form * `TagGroup.Label`. */ export function TagGroupLabel({ className, children, ...props }: TagGroupLabelProps) { return ( {children} ) } /** * The chips. Use it as `TagGroup.List`, wrapping the `TagGroup.Tag`s. * * Exported as `TagGroupList` only so tooling can resolve it; consume the compound form * `TagGroup.List`. */ export function TagGroupList({ className, children, ...props }: TagGroupListProps) { return ( {children} ) } /** * One chip. Use it as `TagGroup.Tag`. Give it an `href` and it is a link rather than a value — the * sheet uses its tags both ways, which is why `Tag` takes `LinkDOMProps`. * * Exported as `TagItem` only so tooling can resolve it; consume the compound form `TagGroup.Tag`. */ export function TagItem({ variant = 'default', href, className, children, ...props }: TagProps) { const inherited = useContext(HREF) const target = href ?? inherited return ( {({ allowsRemoving }) => ( <> {target ? ( // A link needs a wrapper, and a wrapper makes the children "non-plain text" — which is // React Aria's cue to ask for `textValue`, because it can no longer read the name off // the markup. A chip with no destination keeps its text bare and needs nothing. {children} ) : ( children )} {allowsRemoving ? ( ) : null} )} ) } /** * Styled element. Not exported — `TagGroup` below is the public symbol, and docgen reads the JSDoc * from the *exported* declaration, not this one. */ function TagGroupRoot({ className, children, ...props }: TagGroupProps) { return ( {children} ) } /** * The sheet's `.ds-tag`: a 12px uppercase chip, in the seven treatments the sheet defines. * * ```tsx * * * fra1 * iad1 * sfo1 * * * ``` * * Add `selectionMode="multiple"` and the chips become selectable rather than decorative, add a * `href` and they become links — the sheet uses them all three ways, and React Aria decides which * one it is from the props rather than from a different component. * * ### A tag is not a button * * It is a short piece of metadata with an edge. The moment it carries an action, it is a button and * should look like one; the moment it carries nothing but a value, it does not need to be a control * at all. `selectionMode` says the chips are chosen; without it they are labels, and adding * `onRemove` to a group that was never selectable makes a control out of decoration. * * ### Hover deepens the tag's own colour, rather than brightening it * * The sheet's `a.ds-tag:hover { filter: brightness(1.08) }` cannot survive five fills: on a * near-white yellow it is invisible, and on any of them it says nothing about which tag the pointer * is on. Fills deepen toward `--color-ink` — the recipe the button uses — and the two accented * outlines, which have no fill to deepen, take a wash of their own colour instead. Both derive from * the base; neither substitutes a different one. * * The `outline` variant's edge is `--input` rather than the sheet's 35% white, which * measures under the 3:1 a boundary needs on the dark page. It is the same correction the rest of * the system makes, and the reason `--input` exists. */ export const TagGroup = Object.assign(TagGroupRoot, { Label: TagGroupLabel, List: TagGroupList, Tag: TagItem, })

/**
 * The field anatomy, shared by every control that wears it — `TextField`,
 * `SearchField`, and the textarea, select, checkbox and radio still to come.
 *
 * Only the styling lives here. Each component defines its own slot components,
 * thin as they are, so that its docs and manifest describe its own API rather
 * than pointing at another component's.
 */

/**
 * The three control sizes. `size` is set once on the field and travels as two
 * custom properties rather than through React context: the control, and any
 * affix inside it, are ordinary descendants of the field, so inheritance already
 * does the work. It also means a one-off override is just a utility on the
 * element rather than a new prop.
 */
export type FieldSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'

export const FIELD_SIZES: Record<FieldSize, string> = {
  sm: '[--field-control-h:2.25rem] [--field-control-text:0.8125rem]', // 36px / 13px
  md: '[--field-control-h:2.75rem] [--field-control-text:0.875rem]', // 44px / 14px
  lg: '[--field-control-h:3.25rem] [--field-control-text:0.9375rem]', // 52px / 15px
}

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-field`: legend, control, then the hint that explains it.
 *
 * The `font-size` here is what the control and any affix inherit. It sits on the
 * field rather than on the input so it still reaches an affix, which is the
 * input's sibling — a `cap`-sized icon would otherwise match the page's font
 * instead of the field's.
 *
 * The two border properties are published here for the same reason `Checkbox`
 * publishes its own: read-only lives on the field root, while the border it changes
 * is on the input, and a group variant cannot win that cascade — see the note on
 * `INPUT`. Declaring them here means the input only reads them, and the ordinary
 * cascade decides, because `[data-readonly]` plainly outranks the bare declaration.
 */
export const FIELD = [
  'group flex flex-col gap-2 [font-size:var(--field-control-text)]',
  '[--field-border:var(--color-input)]',
  '[--field-hover:var(--color-border)]',
  // Read-only is not disabled: the value is the whole point of the field, so it
  // keeps full-strength text. Only the affordances go — a quieter hairline, and no
  // brightening on hover — because there is nothing here to invite a click on.
  'data-[readonly]:[--field-border:var(--color-border-soft)]',
  'data-[readonly]:[--field-hover:var(--color-border-soft)]',
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-affix` wrapper. `Group` exists for one case: an affix is
 * positioned against the control, but the field also holds the legend and the
 * hint, so an affix anchored to the field would centre on all three.
 * Wrapping the control gives the affix the right box — and it stays opt-in, so a
 * plain field has no extra element at all.
 *
 * The two `:has()` rules are here for the same reason: the room an affix needs is
 * padding on the input, and the group is what can see both of them. The input
 * itself never has to know it has neighbours.
 */
export const GROUP = [
  'relative flex w-full',
  'has-[[data-slot=icon-start]]:[&>[data-slot=input]]:ps-10.5', // 42px, per the sheet's search field
  'has-[[data-slot=icon-end]]:[&>[data-slot=input]]:pe-14', // 56px, per the sheet's trailing unit
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-field-legend`: 12px, uppercase, letterspaced, white 70%.
 *
 * The required marker is drawn from the field's own `data-required`, so the label
 * never has to be told and the asterisk cannot drift out of sync with
 * `isRequired`. The input already carries the native `required`, so this is the
 * visual half of the same fact.
 */
export const LABEL = [
  'text-[12px] uppercase tracking-[0.04em] text-muted-foreground',
  "group-data-[required]:after:ms-1 group-data-[required]:after:text-destructive group-data-[required]:after:content-['*']",
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-input`.
 *
 * The resting hairline is what identifies the control. The sheet gives
 * `.ds-input` a transparent border and leaves the panel-2 fill to do the job, but
 * that fill is 1.23:1 on the dark page and 1.17:1 on the light one, so the field is
 * nearly invisible as a boundary in both. `--input` is the smallest
 * hairline that clears the 3:1 a control boundary needs on each.
 *
 * Hover has to *strengthen* it rather than replace it: the sheet's hover is white
 * at 25%, which is now weaker than the resting line and would erase it.
 *
 * `outline-none` on focus suppresses the *browser's* ring, which is what the
 * sheet's `.ds-input:focus { outline: none }` is really doing. Chrome gives a
 * focused text input its `:focus-visible` ring at `outline-style: auto` regardless
 * of React Aria's attribute, so leaving it alone means a blue UA ring on a teal
 * system. Focus is then the border alone — adding the shared 3px-offset ring here
 * would draw two parallel teal hairlines with a gap, which reads as a fault.
 * `Button` can carry that ring because the edge it repeats is a solid fill.
 */
export const INPUT = [
  // **The corner is a token now, and `rounded-md` is the control step of its scale.** Pulse's own
  // `--radius` is `0`, so the sheet's square field is unchanged here; a theme that sets a radius
  // moves every control in the library at once. See the radius note in `docs/theming.md`.
  'w-full font-mono rounded-md border border-(--field-border)',
  'h-(--field-control-h) px-3.5',
  'bg-muted text-foreground placeholder:text-foreground/35',
  'transition-[border-color,background-color] duration-[120ms] ease-pulse',
  // Focus and invalid stay literal, so they outrank the published border and always
  // win — including on a read-only field, which is still focusable and still the
  // field the caret should be able to reach.
  'data-[hovered]:not-data-[focused]:border-(--field-hover)',
  'data-[focused]:outline-none data-[focused]:border-primary',
  'data-[invalid]:not-data-[focused]:border-destructive',
  'data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed data-[disabled]:opacity-40',
  // Read-only gets the cursor and nothing else that dims it. `opacity` here would
  // take the *value* down with it — at 40% the text measures 3.42:1, under the 4.5:1
  // body text needs, so the one thing the user came to read becomes the thing they
  // cannot.
  'group-data-[readonly]:cursor-not-allowed',
].join(' ')

/** The sheet's `.ds-hint`: 12px, tighter tracking, white 55%. */
export const HINT = 'text-[12px] tracking-[-0.5px] text-foreground/55'

/**
 * The sheet paints its error state yellow, because the original design had only
 * two accents and yellow was the nearest thing to a warning it owned. That does
 * not carry over here: `--warning` is this system's `secondary` button, so
 * errors would be the same colour as a secondary action. The error state uses
 * `--destructive`, the danger hue, and keeps the sheet's flex so an icon can be
 * dropped in front of the message.
 */
export const ERROR =
  'flex items-center gap-1.5 text-[12px] tracking-[-0.5px] text-destructive'

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-affix__unit` and `.ds-affix__icon`: pinned to the control's
 * box, vertically centred, and never a click target — the affix is decoration, and
 * a pointer-events-owning overlay would swallow clicks meant for the field. Sized
 * in `cap` like `Button.Icon`, so one icon works at every field `size`.
 */
export const ICON = [
  'absolute inset-y-0 z-10 grid place-items-center pointer-events-none',
  'text-foreground/70',
  '[&>svg]:block [&>svg]:h-[1.5cap] [&>svg]:w-auto [&>svg]:shrink-0',
].join(' ')

/** The sheet insets both affixes 14px from their edge. */
export const ICON_POSITIONS = {
  start: 'start-3.5',
  end: 'end-3.5',
} as const

export type IconPosition = keyof typeof ICON_POSITIONS

docs:
The sheet's `.ds-tag`: a 12px uppercase chip, in the seven treatments the sheet defines — which is
why there are seven.

```tsx
<TagGroup aria-label="Regions">
  <TagGroup.List>
    <TagGroup.Tag id="fra1" variant="teal">
      fra1
    </TagGroup.Tag>
    <TagGroup.Tag
      id="iad1"
      variant="outline"
      href="/monitors/iad1"
      textValue="iad1"
    >
      iad1
    </TagGroup.Tag>
  </TagGroup.List>
</TagGroup>
```

| Slot             | React Aria | Notes                                    |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `TagGroup`       | `TagGroup` | The set. `selectionMode`, `disabledKeys` |
| `TagGroup.Label` | `Label`    | The sheet's `.ds-field-legend`           |
| `TagGroup.List`  | `TagList`  | The chips, wrapping                      |
| `TagGroup.Tag`   | `Tag`      | One chip. `variant`, `href`, `id`        |

| Variant                  | Sheet              | Treatment                  |
| ------------------------ | ------------------ | -------------------------- |
| _(default)_              | `.ds-tag`          | 70% text, transparent edge |
| `outline`                | `.ds-tag--outline` | an edge at 45%             |
| `teal` `gray` `yellow`   | the three fills    | the fill, carrying `ink`   |
| `outline-ring` `-yellow` | §18's two          | accent edge and text       |

### A selectable or removable chip needs an `id`

`selectedKeys` and `disabledKeys` speak in the tags' `id`s, exactly as `Table.Row` and
`Accordion.Item` do. Without one React Aria generates a key, and `defaultSelectedKeys={['fra1']}`
matches nothing: the story renders, every chip is enabled, and the assertion fails on a missing
attribute rather than on a wrong colour.

### React Aria's `Tag` is a grid row, and provides neither a link nor a remove button

It renders `div[role="row"]` inside `div[role="grid"]` — the same shape as its table and its tree —
and an `href` becomes `data-href` with nothing to click, while `onRemove` becomes
`data-allows-removing` with nothing to press. So `TagGroup.Tag` draws both from the render props: an
anchor when it has an `href`, and a `<Button slot="remove">` when the group allows removing. Same
reason `Table.Selection` writes its own slot — the one attribute that makes it work is the one nobody
remembers.

An early version wrapped every label in a `<span>`, and React Aria answered at runtime: _"A
`textValue` prop is required for `<Tag>` elements with non-plain text children."_ A chip that is not
a link now keeps its text **bare**, so the name can still be read off the markup; only a link, which
needs the wrapper, asks for `textValue`.

### The chip's hover is `:hover`, not `data-hovered`

Everywhere else in this system `data-[hovered]` is right, because React Aria supplies it. `Tag` does
not: a real pointer hover leaves the tag without the attribute, which this component's own test
found. So the chip's hover is the browser's own pseudo-class — correct for a user, and not
reproducible from the test runner. The Hover story was therefore **deleted** rather than written to
assert something else, the same call as the tooltip's hover.

### Hover deepens the tag's own colour

The sheet's `a.ds-tag:hover { filter: brightness(1.08) }` cannot survive five fills: on a near-white
yellow it is invisible, and on any of them it says nothing about _which_ tag the pointer is on. Fills
deepen toward `--ink`, the recipe the button uses; the two accented outlines have no fill to
deepen and take a wash of their own colour instead. Both derive from the base, and the `--tag-hover`
is declared by each variant and read by the base list, so the two land on the same element.

The `outline` edge is `--input` rather than the sheet's 35% white, which measures under
the 3:1 a boundary needs — the correction `--input` exists for.

## Removing a tag is your job, not the component's

**This is the part the docs left out, and it produced a chip with a working remove button that removed
nothing.** `onRemove` is not a command — it is a _report_. React Aria hands you the keys the user asked to
remove and stops there, because the group does not own the collection. A group whose handler does nothing is
a control that does nothing when pressed:

```tsx
// The story shipped this first. The button worked, the tag stayed, and the test passed.
;<TagGroup onRemove={() => {}}>…</TagGroup>

// The pattern to copy: hold the keys, and drop the removed ones.
function Regions() {
  const [keys, setKeys] = useState(['fra1', 'iad1'])
  return (
    <TagGroup
      onRemove={(removed) =>
        setKeys((cur) => cur.filter((k) => !removed.has(k)))
      }
    >
      <TagGroup.List>
        {keys.map((key) => (
          <TagItem key={key} id={key}>
            {key}
          </TagItem>
        ))}
      </TagGroup.List>
    </TagGroup>
  )
}
```

The signature is `(keys: Set<Key>) => void`, so a tag is dropped by filtering on something like
`removed.has(key)` — not by index.

### And the test that missed it

The story counted two remove buttons and checked their accessible names. Both true, both useful, and neither
one presses anything — **a remove control is only proven by the thing being gone.** The story now clicks the
first one and asserts the chip is no longer in the document, that the other one still is, and that the button
count fell. This is the same gap as `ToggleButton`'s off state: an assertion about what was _built_ rather
than about what it _does_.
